name: Starlink V1.0 (original design)
note: Benchmarking M4 reference model for Mallama (2020a), the pre-visor design at 550 km through May 2020. Same chassis as starlink_visorsat.json without the visor or the black edges. Body frame: +Z nadir, +Y toward the Sun's azimuth (the bus yaws so the array is edge-on to the Sun), +X = +Y x +Z. Every number is covered by `sources`; bus_metal and antenna_white are calibrated to MMT tracks (see their sources).

sources.value: bus 1.3 x 2.8 m footprint, 0.2 m thick
sources.source: Footprint: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim (V1.5 row: bus 2.8 x 1.3 m; V1.0 'about 3 m bus', same chassis family). Thickness: 60-satellite stack of 6.7 m in the Falcon 9 fairing (lilibots.blogspot.com, 2020-04, secondary estimate).

sources.subject: antennas
sources.value: white antenna region 0.9 x 2.2 m centred on the nadir face (63% of the base); range 40-80%
sources.source: Cole 2021 (arXiv:2107.06026) section 2 and Figure 1: 'pale/white antenna panels' on a polished-metal base. Region size not published.

sources.subject: solar_array
sources.value: one 2.8 x 8.1 m array standing vertical (shark-fin)
sources.source: McDowell, planet4589.org/astro/starsim (V1.5: solar array 2.8 x 8.1 m); SpaceX: in shark-fin mode 'the solar array goes vertical' (Tesmanian 2020). Hinge at the centre of the bus top: estimate.

sources.subject: bus
sources.value: base to nadir, array edge-on to the Sun's azimuth
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 5: pre-visor Starlinks at 550 km 'are rotated around the nadir-zenith axis ... so the panel is edge-on to the Sun' near the terminator - inferred from ONE image (Vandebergh 2020). Uncertain: the attitude difference from the VisorSat model confounds the visor-only differential.

sources.subject: array
sources.source: SpaceX shark-fin description: 'the solar array goes vertical' (Tesmanian 2020, SpaceX 2020-04-28 update). No fitted tilt is published for the pre-visor design.

sources.subject: bus_metal
sources.value: aluminium, F0 0.9 (preset), Beckmann alpha 0.08, diffuse albedo 0.11, Minnaert k 0.65; also used for the edges
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 2: base is 'polished metal'. F0 0.9 = bare aluminium's normal-incidence reflectance at 550 nm (kept, not fitted). Lobe shape, diffuse floor and the Minnaert exponent are calibrated: starlink_refit 2026-10-22: joint fit, both designs, to 42 Mini-MegaTORTORA tracks (STARLINK-1008 2020/22/24, STARLINK-1436; 1.5-s medians of MMT's magnitude above the atmosphere vs SatModelTool --pass), held out STARLINK-1538 (29 tracks) and STARLINK-1008 2021/23/25 (10); 13 VisorSat bright-attitude tracks excluded (unmodelled attitude). With the GGX tail of the earlier alpha 0.23 (M8, fitted under SatBench's then-assumed Sun -18..-6 deg window, which MMT's -24..-11 does not match) every free fit drove F0 to its floor: MMT sees the base's off-specular tail at phase 75-110 deg ~2x fainter than GGX predicts. A sharp Beckmann lobe (alpha 0.08) reaches that loss with F0 0.9 (Beckmann 0.15: loss +23%). Cole Table 3's exponents 24/52 belong to a BRDF without Fresnel or masking and are not used. Diffuse 0.11: residual contamination / seams. Minnaert k 0.65 on the nadir face's diffuse terms (bus_metal, antenna_white, visor_black): Mallama 2020a's own flat-panel regression on 830 V1.0 passes gives 0.578 +- 0.084; the MMT residual's Sun-altitude trend (Lambert: -0.29 / -0.36 mag per 10 deg, V1.0 / VisorSat fit tracks) is flat at k ~0.55 for V1.0, and the free fit lands at 0.80 (loss 0.1412 vs 0.1426 at 0.65, 0.1439 Lambert): 0.65 is inside Mallama's 1 sigma and takes the trend to -0.07 / -0.22. Section 5: pre-visorsats share the base. Edges: black was ADDED on visorsats (Cole Figure 2), so pre-visor edges are bare metal.

sources.subject: antenna_white
sources.value: white paint preset, diffuse albedo 0.31, Minnaert k 0.65
sources.source: Cole 2021 section 2: 'white antenna panels'. Albedo FITTED (the preset's 0.8 was an estimate): starlink_refit 2026-10-22: joint fit, both designs, to 42 Mini-MegaTORTORA tracks (STARLINK-1008 2020/22/24, STARLINK-1436; 1.5-s medians of MMT's magnitude above the atmosphere vs SatModelTool --pass), held out STARLINK-1538 (29 tracks) and STARLINK-1008 2021/23/25 (10); 13 VisorSat bright-attitude tracks excluded (unmodelled attitude). 0.31 x the 0.9 x 2.2 m region is degenerate with a smaller region at a higher albedo; the region size is unpublished, so the albedo carries it. Minnaert k 0.65 on the nadir face's diffuse terms (bus_metal, antenna_white, visor_black): Mallama 2020a's own flat-panel regression on 830 V1.0 passes gives 0.578 +- 0.084; the MMT residual's Sun-altitude trend (Lambert: -0.29 / -0.36 mag per 10 deg, V1.0 / VisorSat fit tracks) is flat at k ~0.55 for V1.0, and the free fit lands at 0.80 (loss 0.1412 vs 0.1426 at 0.65, 0.1439 Lambert): 0.65 is inside Mallama's 1 sigma and takes the trend to -0.07 / -0.22.
